To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acoustic band gaps in layered structures can be engineered by using finite-size layered materials made of multiple periodicity.

(a) acoustic band-gap structures can be made of two-phase layered structures with only 3–5 cells; (b) by introducing two or more periodicities into the layered structure very sharp passbands can be engineered.

acoustic band gaps in layered structures can be created using very small number of layers, and by introducing two or more periodicities in the structure, very sharp and very broad stop bands can be engineered for the acoustic waves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acoustic band-gap engineering of layered structures with multiple periodicities.
the acoustic properties of a layered structure with multiple periodicity.
the design of layered acoustic structures that have the ability to manipulate acoustic energy in specific frequency ranges.

acoustic band-gap engineering using layered structures of multiple period can be used to design acoustic filters, vibration insulation devices and acoustic mirrors.
